facts.claim: Grant of $50 per 1,000 BTU/h at -8°C for an ENERGY STAR certified air-to-air heat pump, or $120 per 1,000 BTU/h at -8°C if it is certified cold climate. Hydro-Québec advertises up to $6,700. Apply on the LogisVert portal within nine months of installation.
facts.eligibility: Home in Quebec whose main heating runs on electricity; new central split or wall-mounted mini-split system; outdoor unit at least 12,000 BTU/h cooling; bought from a Quebec retailer; installed by an RBQ-licensed company; owners get the grant (tenants are eligible only for the dryer and range). Replacing a failed heat pump, a single coil or unit, and indoor units outside the heated space are not eligible. Off-grid homes cannot use it to replace or add to a fuel-fired heating system.
facts.dates: Participant's guide dated September 15, 2026; no end date stated. Hydro-Québec page says requests are still processed normally after the October 8, 2026 federal announcement.
facts.notes: Guide read as PDF text on 2026-10-10: https://www.hydroquebec.com/data/logisvert/logisvert-guide-participation-residentiel-en.pdf (sections 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, Appendix I). Grant cannot exceed 100% of pre-tax purchase and installation cost. Processing 10 to 12 weeks. Portal is in French only. The $6,700 figure is from the Hydro-Québec page; the guide does not state a cap.

facts.claim: Bonus of $100 per 1,000 BTU/h at -8°C on top of the $120 cold-climate rate, for $220 total, for owners of eligible multi-unit buildings where tenants pay their own electricity.
facts.eligibility: Cold-climate ENERGY STAR wall-mounted mini-split; building in an area Hydro-Québec designates energy insecure (by postal code); built 1995 or earlier; property value per dwelling below the regional median; electric main heating; one meter per home. Condos and businesses are not eligible.
facts.notes: Guide Appendix II. Cannot be combined with the 5% multiple-measure bonus.

facts.claim: 5% added to the total grant when two or more measures are filed in one application (all within the nine-month window).
facts.eligibility: Two or more LogisVert measures in the same application.

facts.program: LogisVert: thermal storage and geothermal (deducted from installer invoice)
facts.claim: $22,000 for an electric thermal storage system plus a central heat pump, $15,000 for a thermal storage system replacing a central heating unit, and $750 per 1,000 BTU/h for a geothermal heat pump. The amount is deducted from the installer's invoice, so no application is filed.
facts.eligibility: Authorized installers only for thermal storage; see Hydro-Québec's installer list.
facts.notes: Replacing an existing geothermal heat pump pays $250 per 1,000 BTU/h (guide: capped at $18,000 per address).

facts.claim: Rénoclimat pays for insulation, air sealing ($400 to $800) and ENERGY STAR doors and windows ($150 each) after an energy assessment, and no longer pays for installing or replacing a heating system. Its rules changed on October 1, 2026; a transition runs to October 12, 2026 for requesting an assessment before work under the old rules.
facts.eligibility: Energy assessment before work required; fees apply.
facts.dates: New rules from October 1, 2026; transition to October 12, 2026.
facts.notes: Heating-system exclusion and LogisVert referral read on https://www.quebec.ca/habitation-territoire/chauffage-consommation-energie/aide-financiere-renovation-ecoenergetique/renoclimat/aide-financiere/subvention-systemes-mecaniques (page dated 2025-10-02). The October 2026 change details were not opened.

facts.program: Federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (Quebec)
facts.claim: July 31, 2026 was the last day to apply. Applications sent before then are still processed; final receipts and the attestation form are due January 31, 2027. Homes in remote areas of Quebec were not eligible.
facts.eligibility: Closed. Applied to oil-heated homes at or below median household after-tax income.
facts.notes: Page lists Quebec among the covered provinces; read 2026-10-10.
